name: Ewoud Van Vooren
summary: 10th-grade student working on electronics, PCB design, and embedded hardware. Seeking a summer 2027 engineering internship with opportunities to build, measure, and debug real hardware.
education: Lincoln-Sudbury Regional High School | Expected graduation: 2029
community: Hardware reviewer for Hack Club’s Half Life program.
New England Sci-Tech volunteer; member of the Northeast HamXposition Youth & Collegiate Activities Committee.

projects.name: DrawBot | CoreXY drawing machine
bullets: Designed and built a half-meter-square pen plotter with CoreXY belts, NEMA17 steppers, a scotch-yoke pen lift, and Arduino Uno R4 WiFi control.
Calibrated motion and pen travel, drew a 100 mm square, and completed a 35-minute drawing run with no BLE drops or command errors. Currently uses manual homing.

projects.name: Ducktop2 | Custom laptop and battery electronics
bullets: Designing an eight-layer motherboard and I/O boards for a 16-inch LattePanda Mu Ultra laptop, including PCIe NVMe, USB, HDMI, Ethernet, and a Wi-Fi socket.
Designed a four-layer BQ76922 battery-management board and ISL9241 charging circuitry for a three-cell battery. Main-board routing is in progress; assembled-board tests are pending.

projects.name: STM32 development board and BLDC motor controller
bullets: Designed a 24 × 44 mm, four-layer STM32F411 board with USB-C, SPI microSD, and SWD; prepared Gerbers, BOM, and component-placement files.
Routed a four-layer STM32G474 motor controller with DRV8353S gate drive, phase-current sensing, and protection circuitry. Both boards await physical bring-up.

projects.name: StratoScience | Balloon instrumentation and image analysis
bullets: Developed Arduino/MPU9250 logging code for timestamped magnetic-field measurements on SD. Credited with the IMU recorder and downward camera on the 2024 StratoScience launch manifest.
Worked on servo-based solar tracking and Python/OpenCV notebooks for matching and aligning balloon and satellite images.

additional: Published 3D World’s Hardest Game in Unity/C# for Windows, macOS, and Linux, and nnzip, a Python text-compression tool, on PyPI. Other builds include a bootable x86 graphing-calculator OS, a 3D-printed RC tank, and Tarmo5 modifications.
skills: KiCad; schematic design; multilayer PCB layout; differential-pair routing; component selection; power electronics; Arduino; soldering; 3D printing; Git and Linux; basic Python and C#.
